name: uswds-ai-components
description: USWDS component registry for AI coding agents building government websites.

highContrast.description: Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode support

darkMode.description: Dark-mode rendering (not yet standard across USWDS components)

compactDensity.description: Dense UI profile with reduced spacing (verify touch targets before use on touch devices)

gaps.nearestAlternative: language-selector tiles (language-selector/default.html, language-selector/expanded.html) or plain links with lang/hreflang (usa.gov Español pattern)
gaps.reason: USWDS has no header-integrated language toggle component; the language-selector tiles cover the standalone list pattern
gaps.consequence: Do not add a header-integrated language toggle; use the language-selector tiles or plain links with lang/hreflang
gaps.source: USWDS language selector component documentation (https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/language-selector/) — USWDS publishes no header-integrated language toggle

gaps.reason: USWDS ships a usa-hero component but the registry has no hero tile yet; compose from section/grid/prose or consult the USWDS hero documentation

gaps.nearestAlternative: the default banner (banner/default.html) or the usa-banner web component, which supports lang, tld, slot=domain-text and --theme-banner-background-color but no size attribute
gaps.reason: USWDS 3 ships no slim or medium banner variant; those sizes are USWDS 2.x legacy. The tiles that documented them carried non-canonical markup: no usa-accordion wrapper, no toggle button, and a div in place of header.usa-banner__header
gaps.consequence: Do not build a slim or medium banner. Use the default banner or the usa-banner web component, and express any compact styling as scoped site CSS — never a usa-banner--slim or usa-banner--medium class
gaps.source: USWDS banner component documentation (https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/banner/) renders only usa-banner and usa-banner site-banner; no size modifier exists in the 3.14.0 stylesheet

gaps.nearestAlternative: the default breadcrumb (breadcrumb/default.html) for hierarchy, or plain links for sequential prev/next navigation
gaps.reason: USWDS ships no prev/next breadcrumb variant. The class such a tile implied (usa-breadcrumb--naviprev-next) does not exist in the 3.14.0 stylesheet, and the component page documents only default, RDFa-metadata and truncated variants
gaps.consequence: Do not build a prev/next breadcrumb. Use the default breadcrumb for hierarchy, or plain links labelled Previous/Next — never a usa-breadcrumb--naviprev-next class
gaps.source: USWDS breadcrumb component documentation renders Default, RDFa metadata and Truncated previews only; no naviprev-next class in the 3.14.0 stylesheet

gaps.nearestAlternative: the default icon list (icon-list/default.html) — choose the icon itself to convey checklist meaning, and size icons with usa-icon--size-* on the svg
gaps.reason: usa-icon-list--checklist and usa-icon-list--icon-lg do not exist in the 3.14.0 stylesheet. The component page documents Default, Simple content, Rich content and Custom size previews, none of which use those classes
gaps.consequence: Do not add usa-icon-list--checklist or usa-icon-list--icon-lg. Express a checklist by selecting a check icon, and custom sizes via usa-icon--size-* on the icon svg
gaps.source: USWDS icon list component documentation previews (Default, Simple content, Rich content, Custom size); neither class appears in the 3.14.0 stylesheet

gaps.nearestAlternative: side-navigation/sidenav.html or side-navigation/current.html — both nest a plain ul.usa-sidenav__sublist inside li.usa-sidenav__item
gaps.reason: usa-nav__submenu is header navigation markup, not side navigation. Side navigation nests ul.usa-sidenav__sublist inside li.usa-sidenav__item with no toggle; there is no expandable variant. The retired tile used usa-nav, usa-nav__primary, usa-nav__primary-item, usa-nav__link and usa-nav__submenu while claiming to be side navigation
gaps.consequence: Do not use usa-nav__* classes inside a side navigation. Nest ul.usa-sidenav__sublist inside li.usa-sidenav__item; for header dropdowns use the header tiles instead
gaps.source: USWDS side navigation examples nest ul.usa-sidenav__sublist inside li.usa-sidenav__item; usa-nav__submenu appears only in header navigation markup

gaps.concept: summary box severity variants (info / warning / error)
gaps.nearestAlternative: summary-box/default.html for a neutral key-information panel; alert/error.html for an error summary; site-alert tiles for site-wide status messages
gaps.reason: USWDS ships exactly one summary box. The component page has a single Default preview and the 3.14.0 stylesheet defines only usa-summary-box, __heading, __text and __link — no severity modifiers. The retired tiles were structurally identical to the default tile and differed only in heading wording
gaps.consequence: Do not build info, warning or error summary boxes. Use summary-box/default for neutral key information, alert/error for an error summary, and the site-alert tiles for site-wide status
gaps.source: USWDS summary box documentation has one Default preview; no severity modifier exists in the 3.14.0 stylesheet. Error summaries in USWDS are usa-alert--error, tiled at alert/error.html

gaps.nearestAlternative: the USWDS data visualization guidance (designsystem.digital.gov/components/data-visualizations) plus your chosen charting library; the registry tiles demonstrate one accessible pattern but are origin: extension, not canon
gaps.reason: USWDS states the data visualizations components are guidance-only and do not include any Component Code. There are no usa-chart classes in the 3.14.0 stylesheet; the tiles use registry-internal demo classes in the USWDS namespace
gaps.consequence: Do not present usa-chart or usa-chart-container as USWDS classes. Choose a charting library, follow the USWDS guidance for accessible charts (text alternative, data table, colour contrast), and treat the tiles as one worked example
gaps.source: USWDS data visualizations page: "The data visualizations components are guidance-only and do not include any Component Code"; no usa-chart class in the 3.14.0 stylesheet

banner.note: the banner is a <section aria-label>, not a generic div (usa-banner.twig; _notifications.scss `section.usa-banner`)

site-alert.note: usa-site-alert.twig: <section class="usa-site-alert" aria-label> — a labelled region

identifier.note: usa-identifier.twig: the identifier root is <div class="usa-identifier">
usa-identifier.twig: the identity block is <section class="usa-identifier__identity">

accordion.note: usa-accordion.twig + the JS BUTTON selector: the control must be a <button>, or the toggle is inert

file-input.note: file-input JS removes usa-file-input from the input and adds it to a created parent wrapper at init; the input keeps usa-file-input__input. Tiles are authored in that post-init state, which is the structure the stylesheet targets

staticView.note: Resolved-view generation input (see _base/generate-resolved-view.mjs). Design-system CSS injected at build time because USWDS tiles rely on external USWDS styles per tile-format.md self-containment exception.

allowlist.reason: Documented USWDS character-count markup (official usa-character-count.twig); behavior hook for usa-character-count.js, no styles in the bundle
Documented USWDS character-count markup (official usa-character-count.twig); JS creates the live status regions from it, unstyled in the 3.14 bundle
Documented USWDS 3.14 backward-compat no-op (breadcrumbs wrap by default; class has no effect)
